notes: This map states what a user can observe and what is not covered. It does not state the expected values: those live in verify-items.js, because a feature document that recorded them would be a second place for a behaviour regression to edit.

features.behavior: A service that has never been written to answers GET /items with an empty list rather than an error or a missing field.
setup: start the service with a state file that does not yet exist

features.behavior: An item created by POST /items appears in the list returned by a later GET /items. Neither request is interesting alone; the behaviour is that the second observes the effect of the first.
setup: start the service with a fresh state file
POST /items over HTTP, then GET /items over HTTP

features.behavior: Items are listed in the order they were created, and creating more does not replace what was there.
setup: create one item, then a second, then read the list

features.behavior: A request that would create an unusable item is refused, and the refusal leaves the stored list exactly as it was.
setup: create two items, then attempt one with an empty name, then read the list

features.behavior: A route the service does not implement is refused with a not-found answer rather than being treated as an empty list.
setup: start the service and request a route that does not exist

features.behavior: Two instances running at the same time hold separate item lists, so one instance never reads what another was given.
setup: start two instances, each on a port the operating system assigned
write to one, read from both

features.behavior: Changing an item that already exists replaces its stored value.
setup: create an item, then send a request intended to change it
coverage_gaps: the service has no update route; this is a feature the product has not built and it is recorded here so its absence is visible rather than assumed

features.behavior: Two requests that create an item at the same instant both end up in the list.
setup: issue overlapping POST /items requests against one instance
coverage_gaps: the state file is read and rewritten per request, so overlapping writes can lose one; no check exercises this, and the feature is unverified for that reason
